column1: # PURPOSE: every resource cited or used in this project, in a form that can be fed to the
# memory/knowledge store later without re-scraping and without re-deriving provenance.
# FORMAT: tab-separated. One row per source. Header row is normative — the column set is the
# schema. Do NOT reorder columns; append new ones at the end and bump SCHEMA.
#   id            stable slug; cite this from prose. Never reuse, never repurpose.
#   kind          paper | repo | doc | vendor | standard | blog | dataset
#   url           canonical URL (prefer DOI/arXiv abstract over PDF)
#   license       SPDX-ish where known; "unknown" is a real value and must not be guessed
#   tier          primary | secondary | unverified   (see TIERS below)
#   claims        comma-separated claim ids this source supports (see CLAIMS.tsv)
#   date_checked  ISO date the URL/claim was last actually fetched (not assumed)
#   notes         one line; caveats, corrections, why it matters
#   primary     — the artifact itself: paper abstract/PDF, repo metadata via API, spec, vendor doc.
#   secondary   — a third-party summary used only for orientation, never as sole support.
#   unverified  — seen referenced but NOT fetched from a primary source. MUST NOT be cited as fact.
#   1. A source is `verified` only if `date_checked` reflects an actual fetch in this session.
#   2. `unverified` rows are retained deliberately — they are the anti-recurrence list. Never delete;
#   3. Never guess a license. "unknown" is correct and useful.
#   4. Licenses matter here: the project adopts ideas-not-code, and TS+Rust only. A permissive
#      license does not make Python adoptable, and a copyleft license does not block reading.

column3: Multiple-Baseline Designs (instructional module)
column13: READ IN FULL. Multiple-baseline across behaviours "requires at least two separate behaviours that are INDEPENDENT of one another. In other words, as the intervention is applied to one behaviour, the other behaviour(s) should REMAIN AT THE SAME BASELINE LEVELS." If the second improves during baseline, "the experimental control is compromised and an extraneous variable is a possible cause." Three variants: across behaviours, participants, settings.

column3: Multiple-baseline design (clinical glossary, sources-checked)
column13: READ IN FULL, with linked primary sources named. THE DECISIVE SOURCE FOR Q1h. Key rules: tiers must be "similar enough that the SAME INTERVENTION AND MEASURE MAKE SENSE" and independent enough that treatment in one does not change another before its start. WWC three-demonstration convention: at least THREE TIERS with phase changes at three different points in time. Concurrent vs NONCONCURRENT variants distinguished; nonconcurrent is legitimate but "shared history events become harder to evaluate across tiers". "Meeting a tier count cannot rescue dependent tiers or an invalid measure." Requires recording calendar dates, baseline duration and TIER-SPECIFIC EVENTS. Missing observations stay visible with reason. Early change is recorded as GENERALIZATION. Also cites WWC SCD Technical Documentation, SCRIBE 2016, Onghena & Edgington, Slocum et al., Smith.

SRC-081 is the the host harness session-log CORPUS CENSUS (a census of ~/.host harness/sessions read to establish confounder axes); this row is this workspace's OWN BUILD-VERIFICATION MEASUREMENT PASS of 2026-09-29, whose subject is the cockpit code and the store it writes, not the corpus. Kept as a separate row precisely so the two are never conflated: the CLM-CONF-11 precedent is a claim measured against SRC-081, and these two are measured against this row. EVIDENCE, ALL INSIDE THIS REPO: (1) the store, app/data/observation/2026-09-29.jsonl, 344 MB, 433,269 _op=put lines - the target of both defects and the artifact in which both post-fix conditions are re-checkable; (2) the adapter under test, app/src/adapters/host harness.ts (BoundaryGate class :209-259, gate open :564, admits call site :688, inclusive per-event gates :901/:972/:1011, derived ts at :981 and :1018, file skip :609, effectiveSince :621); (3) the cursor computation that feeds it, app/src/plugins/adapters.ts:132-135 and :139, which sets the next cursor to the max ts of everything the previous poll yielded; (4) the regression tests, app/tests/host harness-adapter.spec.ts, including the silent-drop case at :761-809 asserting 'session-ancient'. RE-MEASURED FOR THE EDIT THAT CREATED THIS ROW, NOT TAKEN ON REPORT: a streaming scan of all 433,269 put lines returned 433,269 put / 433,256 distinct ids / excess 13, with all 13 repeated ids appearing exactly TWICE and differing in provenance (a legitimate supersede from a forced second poll) and ZERO byte-identical re-appends; the id that had been appended 34 times pre-fix, b47f493f-32e5-4aa4-8ed4-74e9d7d799f8:step:1:13, now occurs exactly once, at _seq 425724. SO THIS ROW IS primary and verified on the same footing as SRC-081: the artifacts are local, but they were read, not assumed. SCOPE LIMIT, STATED SO IT IS NOT READ AS A CORPUS CENSUS: this row covers the cockpit adapter and store only. It makes no claim about ~/.host harness, asserts no confounder axis, and its figures are bound to a store snapshot on 2026-09-29 that a re-ingest will not reproduce exactly. READ-ONLY: nothing under ~/.host harness was read for this row beyond the corpus SRC-081 already covers, and no file outside this repo was created, modified or deleted.
